ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a geometric figure composed of multiple blue line segments. The lower-left angle of the large triangle is labeled ∠1, the vertex angle is labeled ∠8, and both of these angles have pink arc markings, indicating ∠1≅∠8. At the lower-right vertex, there is a horizontal base extended to the right, and an exterior angle 130° is marked; from the left intersection point to the lower-right vertex there is a diagonal line, and at the lower-right vertex, 30° is marked between this diagonal line and the right slanted side. Near the left intersection point there are ∠3, ∠4, ∠6; at the upper-right intersection point there are 110°, ∠7, ∠5. It is required to find ∠4. Reasoning: At the lower-right vertex, 130° is the exterior angle formed by the extension of the base and the diagonal line, so the interior angle forming a linear pair with it is 180°−130°=50°. Adding the 30° marked at the lower right, the total angle at the lower-right corner of the large triangle is 50°+30°=80°. In the large triangle, the other two angles are ∠1 and ∠8, and ∠1≅∠8, so ∠1=∠8=(180°−80°)/2=50°. Next look at the lower-left small triangle, in which ∠1=50°, and the angle formed by the base and the diagonal line at the lower right is also 50°, so ∠3 at the left intersection point =180°−50°−50°=80°. At the upper-right intersection point, ∠7 and 110° are supplementary angles, so ∠7=180°−110°=70°. Next look at the upper small triangle, ∠8=50°, ∠7=70°, so ∠6 at the left intersection point =180°−50°−70°=60°. Finally, at the left intersection point, ∠6, ∠4, ∠3 are on one side of the same straight line and sum to 180°, therefore ∠4=180°−60°−80°=40°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: the pink arcs show ∠1 ≅ ∠8; at the right-bottom vertex the 130° is an exterior angle on the base extension, the 30° is between the diagonal to the left intersection and the right side, and ∠4 is the angle at the left intersection between the upper-right slanted line and the lower-right slanted line. Then angle-chase as follows: the interior angle at the right-bottom vertex in triangle BTR is 180°−130° = 50° for the base/diagonal part, and adding the marked 30° gives the full triangle angle there as 80°. So in triangle BTR, ∠1 and ∠8 are the other two angles, and since they are marked congruent, each is (180°−80°)/2 = 50°. Next, in triangle BOR, the angles at B and R are both 50°, so the angle at O on the lower side is ∠3 = 80°. At the top-right intersection, ∠7 is supplementary to the 110° angle, so ∠7 = 70°. In triangle TOP, ∠8 = 50° and ∠7 = 70°, so ∠6 = 60°. Finally, along the straight line through the left intersection, ∠6 + ∠4 + ∠3 = 180°, hence ∠4 = 180°−60°−80° = 40°.
